newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian citizens' groups hail election deal.
newsitem.headline: Albanian citizens' groups hail election deal.

text.p: Leaders of Albania's so-called Salvation Committees met on Sunday and hailed an agreement signed by political parties on elections.

Under the agreement, brokered by European envoy Franz Vranitzky last week, the committees have to disband by May 14 but they reiterated that a bigger meeting on May 16 would decide the future of the groups.

The citizens' groups were formed to restore order after rioting erupted in southern Albania earlier this year over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes. They blame President Sali Berisha for the collapse of the schemes and want him to quit.
Their leaders met to discuss the deal brokered by Vranitzky, head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), and signed by the 10 key parties.
"The participants in the consultation hail the political contract of the parties and define it as an important step to solve the Albanian crisis," said a statement released after the meeting.
The deal committed the parties to deciding a new electoral law by Monday and passing it through parliament so Berisha can sign a decree by May 15 to order an election.

"We (have) invited the 10 parties on May 16 and representatives of the OSCE and we want to ask them if there will really be free and fair political elections," said Xhevat Kocia, chairman of the committee in the town of Sarande.
"They should assure us this would happen. Every future government should guarantee to us the return of the money (from the pyramid schemes) and the departure of Berisha from power," he added.
